title: extract@v1
description: Structured extraction from a single source document (SPEC §5). One per source; assembled into collection<extract@v1> by the map node. Carries what a traceable requirements document needs: every item names its source and, where the source states it in words, quotes those words.

source.description: Human-readable identifier of this source — the file name as it will appear in the requirements document's source index.

source_type.description: What KIND of document this is. It sets how much weight its statements carry: a signed request for proposals is not a chat log. Shown in the document index.

requirements.description: Discrete requirements found in the source. Empty is valid: a source that states none is a real answer.

text.description: One clear, self-contained requirement sentence, in the language of the source.

domain.description: The business area this belongs to: authentication, booking, notifications, reporting. The requirements document groups its sections by these, so naming it here is what makes that grouping possible.

priority.description: MUST only when the source treats it as essential. A document whose every requirement is MUST has prioritised nothing.

quote.description: The source's own words for this requirement, verbatim, when it states it in words. This is what makes the requirement checkable: a later stage holds the written requirement against the quote and sees whether they say the same thing. Omit only when the source carries it as a table cell, a diagram or a checkbox with no sentence to quote.

locator.description: Where in the source it sits: sheet and row, page, section heading, timestamp. What a reader needs to find it again.

measure.description: The number the source gives, if any: 1000 users, under 200 ms, seven years of retention. A non-functional requirement without one cannot be tested.

stakeholders.description: Roles the source names, with what the source says they do.

tentative.description: True when the role appears only in passing: a box in a diagram, an unexplained word. Lets the document mark it unconfirmed instead of inventing a job for it.

business_context.description: Facts about the business that are not requirements but decide how requirements are read: the model, the market, the deadline, what a previous vendor left behind.

data_entities.description: Things the system stores, as the source names them, with the attributes it mentions.

integrations.description: External systems the source says this one must talk to.

out_of_scope.description: What the source explicitly EXCLUDES. A scope boundary someone stated is as load-bearing as a requirement, and it is the first thing lost when nobody writes it down.

internal_conflicts.description: Places where this ONE source contradicts itself: a sheet marking a feature both in scope and out. Report it here rather than picking a side. The contradiction is a finding, and resolving it belongs to the stage that sees every source at once.

decisions.description: Decisions the source records as already made.

constraints.description: Technical, budget, timeline or regulatory constraints.

open_questions.description: Gaps and ambiguities to resolve later; prefer flagging over guessing.

trust_level.description: Confidence in this extraction given the source's clarity.
